notes: default_days is the number the form fills in when the blank is left empty. null means the form leaves it to negotiation (blank, no fallback) or that no default could be confirmed; the notes field says which.

verify:true means the figure was not confirmed from the association or regulator's own form text. Many association forms are members-only (C.A.R., AAR, NWMLS, MAR, VAR), so their figures come from secondary sources or older versions.
Standard forms are revised often, some twice a year. Check the footer revision of the form actually being used.

general.summary: National consumer sources most often put the inspection contingency at 7-10 days. Chase says about two weeks, and California's default runs 17 days. Texas uses a paid, negotiated option period instead of a classic contingency.

sources.name: Rocket Mortgage - Inspection contingency guide (usually 7-10 days)
Redfin - Top home-buying contingencies (home inspection 7-10 days; CA up to 17 days)
Chase - Home inspection contingency (generally two weeks)

states.name: California
states.form: C.A.R. Residential Purchase Agreement and Joint Escrow Instructions (RPA)
states.form_version_or_date: Latest public version found: RPA revised 6/25. A December 2025 forms release was scheduled; current revision unconfirmed.
states.starts: Days after Acceptance (DAA); day of acceptance not counted
states.notes: Buyer removes the investigation contingency 17 (or ___) days after Acceptance. Per C.A.R.'s RPA timelines guide, 'days = calendar days, unless otherwise specified'. Contingencies are not waived automatically when the period ends: the seller may serve a Notice to Buyer to Perform, at the earliest 15 DAA for the 17-day items. The RPA sets no seller response deadline for a Request for Repair. C.A.R. form text is members-only.

states.name: Texas
states.form: TREC One to Four Family Residential Contract (Resale)
states.form_version_or_date: TREC No. 20-19 (replaces 20-18), effective 07/01/2026
states.starts: Days after the Effective Date
states.notes: Paragraph 5B Termination Option: the buyer may terminate 'within ___ days after the Effective Date of this contract (Option Period)'. The number of days and the option fee are negotiated; there is no default. The option fee is due within 3 days after the Effective Date, and that deadline rolls past a Saturday, Sunday or Legal Holiday. Termination notice must be given by 5:00 p.m. local time. 'Time is of the essence... strict compliance... is required.' If no option fee is stated or it is not delivered on time, the buyer has no unrestricted termination right. There is no seller response period; repairs are negotiated by amendment.

states.name: Florida
states.form: Florida Realtors/Florida Bar "AS IS" Residential Contract for Sale and Purchase (ASIS) and the FR/Bar standard Residential Contract for Sale and Purchase
states.form_version_or_date: FloridaRealtors/FloridaBar-ASIS-7x. A 2026 redline was posted Feb 2026; the footer shows Rev. 12/24 with 2026 revision markings.
states.starts: Days after Effective Date
states.notes: AS IS paragraph 12(a): 'Buyer shall have ___ (if left blank, then 15) days after Effective Date ("Inspection Period")'. The buyer may cancel in sole discretion by written notice before the period expires. Time paragraph: 'Calendar days... shall be used in computing time periods.' A period ending on a Saturday, Sunday or national legal holiday extends to the next such business day. The FR/Bar standard (repair-obligation) contract also uses a 15-day default Inspection Period (secondary sources), with seller repair limits defaulting to 1.5% of purchase price per category. Florida Realtors' own CRSP-17 contract (not a Bar form) defaults the Inspection Period to the earlier of 10 days after Effective Date or 10 days before Closing.

states.name: Georgia
states.form: GAR F201 Purchase and Sale Agreement
states.form_version_or_date: 2023 version (01/01/23) seen; GAR issues annual revisions (2026 forms exist). Current F201 not fetched.
states.starts: Days from the Binding Agreement Date
states.notes: Due Diligence Period of ___ days from the Binding Agreement Date, negotiated with no default. During the period the buyer may terminate for any reason. Related forms: F710 Amendment to Change the Due Diligence Period; F704 Amendment to Address Concerns with Property.

states.name: North Carolina
states.form: NC REALTORS / NC Bar Offer to Purchase and Contract (Standard Form 2-T)
states.form_version_or_date: Standard Form 2-T Revised 7/2025 (a marked-up 7/2026 revision is posted by NC REALTORS)
states.starts: Begins on the Effective Date; ends 5:00 p.m. on the stated date or after the stated number of days
states.notes: Paragraph 1(f): the Due Diligence Period runs from the Effective Date through 5:00 p.m. on a date inserted, or a number of days after the Effective Date. It is negotiated and the form says 'not N/A'. The Due Diligence Fee is negotiated and optional, and is due the next banking day. Paragraph 22: 'days' means consecutive calendar days including weekends and holidays, counted from the day after the triggering event. The buyer may terminate for any or no reason during the period.

states.name: Colorado
states.form: Colorado Real Estate Commission Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate (Residential) (CBS1)
states.form_version_or_date: Adopted August 5, 2025; mandatory use January 1, 2026 (replaces CBS1-6-24)
states.starts: Deadlines entered as dates (or days) in the Dates and Deadlines table
states.notes: No preprinted default. Inspection Objection Deadline, Inspection Termination Deadline and Inspection Resolution Deadline are negotiated entries in the contract's Dates and Deadlines section. If the buyer objects (NTC43) and no written resolution is signed by the Inspection Resolution Deadline, the contract terminates unless the buyer withdraws the objection. Calendar-day counting was not confirmed from the 2026 CBS1 text because the Division of Real Estate site blocked the fetch.

states.name: Arizona
states.form: Arizona Association of REALTORS (AAR) Residential Resale Real Estate Purchase Contract
states.form_version_or_date: Updated November 2025; February 2026 redline posted
states.starts: Days after Contract acceptance
states.notes: 'Buyer's Inspection Period shall be ten (10) days or ___ days after Contract acceptance' (10/22 form text). An AAR legal hotline ruling counted Christmas Day and Christmas Day Observed inside the 10 days, so holidays are not excluded. The seller has 5 days after receiving the BINSR to respond, per secondary sources citing Section 6f. Then the buyer may cancel or accept the seller's response. The current form text was not fetched because aaronline.com returned 403.

states.name: Washington
states.form: NWMLS Form 35 Inspection Addendum (used with Form 21 Residential Purchase and Sale Agreement)
states.form_version_or_date: Rev. 2/26 reported by a secondary source; NWMLS forms are members-only
states.starts: Day after mutual acceptance; deadlines expire 9:00 p.m. Pacific
states.notes: Inspection period is 10 days if left blank, with an additional-inspection period of 5 days if the inspector recommends more in writing. The 2015 form text shows a 3-day default for the seller response and a 3-day default for the buyer reply. Buyer inaction waives the contingency. Requests and responses go on Form 35R. One practitioner blog describes the defaults as business days; calendar is shown here per the Form 21 counting convention, but this is unconfirmed.

states.name: Virginia
states.form: Virginia REALTORS Residential Sales Contract with Form 600D Home Inspection Contingency Addendum (Northern Virginia uses the NVAR K1321 Residential Sales Contract)
states.form_version_or_date: 600D 2019-01 version seen; NVAR K1321 draft 07/26 posted
states.starts: Days after Date of Ratification
states.notes: Form 600D: the contract is contingent until ___ days after the Date of Ratification (the Home Inspection Deadline), negotiated. The deadline can be extended up to 5 days for additional inspections if the buyer gives notice. A Negotiation Period follows any repair request; its length and the buyer's post-negotiation termination window are blanks. An older NVAR contract changed its inspection period from 5 to 7 days, but that figure may be outdated.

states.name: Illinois
states.form: Multi-Board Residential Real Estate Contract 8.0 (replaced 7.0)
states.form_version_or_date: v8.0 (Chicago Association of REALTORS highlighted-changes release, Jan/Feb 2025)
states.starts: Business Days after Date of Acceptance
states.notes: Attorney Review (para 13): 5 Business Days after Date of Acceptance. Inspection with requests: the buyer serves notice of major-component defects within 5 Business Days after Date of Acceptance (10 calendar days for lead-based paint). If no written agreement is reached by 10 Business Days after Date of Acceptance, either party may terminate. Business Days are Monday-Friday excluding Federal holidays; Business Hours are 8 a.m.-6 p.m. Chicago time. The separate Chicago Association of REALTORS Residential Real Estate Purchase and Sale Contract (Rev. 12/2024) leaves both attorney approval and inspection as blank business-day counts.

states.name: New York
states.form: No single statewide REALTOR purchase contract. NYC uses attorney-drafted contracts (e.g., the bar-association Residential Contract of Sale); upstate boards use contracts with an attorney approval contingency.
states.form_version_or_date: Varies by board
states.starts: Upstate: business days after attorney's receipt of the signed contract
states.notes: Upstate attorney-approval clauses commonly give 3 business days (Moran v. Erk, NY Court of Appeals). Either attorney may disapprove for any or no reason. In New York City, buyers typically inspect and do due diligence before signing the contract, so there is usually no post-signing inspection contingency. This is practice, not a form default.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.form: Pennsylvania Association of REALTORS Standard Agreement for the Sale of Real Estate (ASR)
states.form_version_or_date: Current ASR revision not fetched (PAR forms are members-only)
states.starts: Days after Execution Date (last signature = day 0)
states.notes: Inspection Contingency (para 13(A)): the Contingency Period is the number of days inserted, or 10 days if left blank. The seller has 5 days from the END of the contingency period, not from receipt of the buyer's Written Corrective Proposal, to say whether it will satisfy the proposal. If the seller does not agree, the buyer has 2 days to terminate or accept. PAR commentary says all days count the same, with no business-day or holiday exception.

states.name: Ohio
states.form: Ohio REALTORS Residential Purchase Contract (local boards such as Columbus REALTORS publish their own)
states.form_version_or_date: Ohio REALTORS form, copyright 2022
states.starts: From the Date of Acceptance; 'Day(s) after Acceptance' starts 12:01 a.m. the first day following
states.notes: Para 9.B: inspections must be completed within ___ days (10 days if left blank) from the Date of Acceptance, or they are deemed waived. Para 9.C: the buyer may terminate or request a remedy only for material defects. After a request to remedy, the parties have ___ days (3 days if left blank) to reach a written agreement (Remedy Period). 'Days' means calendar day(s), including holidays, Eastern Time. Columbus REALTORS (RES13 02/25) uses its own form with different blanks.

states.name: Michigan
states.form: No single statewide form; local REALTOR boards and brokerages publish their own buy-and-sell agreements
states.form_version_or_date: Varies
states.starts: Typically days after acceptance (form-specific)
states.notes: Michigan REALTORS guidance uses a 10-day sample clause and warns that forms differ on whether buyer silence waives the contingency or terminates the agreement. Examples in its materials and case law use 10, 14 and 15 days. No statewide default.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.form: Standard Form Offer to Purchase Real Estate (e.g., MAR / GBREB forms), followed by a Purchase and Sale Agreement
states.form_version_or_date: Varies; not fetched
states.starts: Days after the offer is accepted/signed
states.notes: The inspection contingency is typically 7-10 days in the Offer to Purchase. Buyers usually finish inspections before signing the P&S, and the contingency is then deleted from the P&S. A signed standard-form offer is binding under Massachusetts case law. 760 CMR 74.00 restricts sellers from conditioning acceptance on the buyer waiving a home inspection; one blog reports this effective October 2025.

states.name: Tennessee
states.form: Tennessee REALTORS RF401 Purchase and Sale Agreement
states.form_version_or_date: 2023 forms-changes packet (RF401 copyright 2015 base); current revision not fetched
states.starts: Days after the Binding Agreement Date
states.notes: Inspection Period: 'Within ___ days after the Binding Agreement Date', negotiated. Delivering a written repair list or Repair/Replacement Proposal ends the Inspection Period and starts a Resolution Period of ___ days, also negotiated, during which the parties negotiate in good faith. 'Day(s)' are calendar days ending at 11:59 p.m. local time.

states.name: Nevada
states.form: Greater Las Vegas Association of REALTORS (GLVAR) Residential Purchase Agreement (Northern Nevada: Sierra Nevada REALTORS form)
states.form_version_or_date: GLVAR RPA Rev. 03/23 (file posted 10/2023); a Rev. 10/24 is referenced by secondary sources
states.starts: Calendar days following the date of Acceptance
states.notes: Section 7(A): 'Buyer shall have ___ calendar days following the date of Acceptance' to complete Due Diligence, negotiated. By the Due Diligence Deadline the buyer must cancel or resolve objections in writing with the seller, or the Due Diligence Condition is deemed waived.

states.name: Oregon
states.form: OREF 001 Residential Real Estate Sale Agreement; Oregon REALTORS Form 1.1 Oregon Residential Real Estate Purchase and Sale Agreement
states.form_version_or_date: Form 1.1 Version 2024-2; OREF 001 version not fetched
states.starts: Business days after mutual acceptance / Effective Date
states.notes: The 10 Business Day default comes from secondary sources (closing-agent guide), not confirmed from the form. Oregon REALTORS warns that written disapproval is due by midnight on the last day of the Inspection Period unless properly extended. Separately, Oregon law gives buyers 5 business days after receiving the Seller's Property Disclosure Statement to revoke.

states.name: Utah
states.form: Utah Division of Real Estate state-approved Real Estate Purchase Contract (REPC)
states.form_version_or_date: New REPC effective November 1, 2026 (old form usable through December 31, 2026)
states.starts: Due Diligence Deadline is a calendar date negotiated in the REPC deadlines section
states.notes: No default: the Due Diligence Deadline is a negotiated date. Performance is due by 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Only earnest-money dates and the Settlement Deadline roll to the next business day if they fall on a weekend or holiday. Late seller disclosures do not automatically extend the Due Diligence Deadline; a written addendum is required. The REPC text was not fetched because the DRE server refused the connection.

states.name: New Jersey
states.form: New Jersey REALTORS Standard Form of Real Estate Contract (Form 118) with attorney review clause required by N.J.A.C. 11:5-6.2
states.form_version_or_date: Current form revision not fetched
states.starts: Three business days from delivery of the signed contract to the parties (delivery day not counted)
states.notes: The 3 business days is the attorney review period, not the inspection period. Either party's attorney may disapprove within 3 business days; weekends and holidays are excluded. Notice by overnight mail is effective on mailing (Conley v. Guerrero, 2017). The inspection contingency is typically added or adjusted during attorney review; secondary sources describe 10-14 days after attorney review ends. The form's inspection default was not confirmed.

states.name: Maryland
states.form: Maryland REALTORS Residential Contract of Sale with Property Inspections Addendum
states.form_version_or_date: Current revision not fetched
states.starts: Days from the Date of Contract Acceptance
states.notes: The contract requires any home or environmental inspection contingency to be placed in an addendum. The Property Inspections Addendum text and its notice and negotiation deadlines could not be retrieved. For comparison, the Greater Capital Area (DC/MD suburbs) Addendum of Clauses has a 3-day seller response, where silence means the buyer's latest notice is accepted.
